display.purpose: Page titles via .brand-heading; Space Grotesk 600, in-app.

headline.purpose: Large marketing-style display headlines; rarely used in-app.

label.purpose: Captions, metadata, badges, form labels; uppercase eyebrow only for nav groups.

shadows.name: card-rest
shadows.purpose: shadow-xs on cards, card-base, primary buttons — the default rest lift.

shadows.name: section-card-wash
shadows.purpose: Soft colored downward glow under tinted section cards; colored variants swap the hue.

shadows.name: sidebar-edge
shadows.purpose: Soft right-edge shadow on the nav rail.

shadows.name: hover-glow
shadows.purpose: Constrained ambient halo on interactive hover (.hover-glow-*).

shadows.name: inset-top-card
shadows.purpose: Single-pixel top sheen on raised card surfaces.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out; default for all state transitions and entrances.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The highest-contrast object on screen — white-on-black in dark mode, black-on-white in light.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 40px; padding: 0 16px; border: 0; border-radius: 10px; background: hsl(var(--primary)); color: hsl(var(--primary-foreground)); font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.01em; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.05); transition: background-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), box-shadow 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: hsl(var(--primary) / 0.9); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: hsl(var(--ring)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px hsl(var(--ring) / 0.5); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.98); } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { pointer-events: none; opacity: 0.5; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Bordered control with a constrained backdrop-blur; hover tightens the border toward primary.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 40px; padding: 0 16px; border: 1px solid hsl(var(--border) / 0.8); border-radius: 10px; background: hsl(var(--background) / 0.75); color: hsl(var(--foreground)); font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.01em; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.05); backdrop-filter: blur(4px); transition: border-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), background-color 200ms, color 200ms; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { border-color: hsl(var(--primary) / 0.35); background: hsl(var(--accent) / 0.7); color: hsl(var(--accent-foreground)); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: hsl(var(--ring)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px hsl(var(--ring) / 0.5); } .ds-btn-outline:active { transform: scale(0.98); }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: No border, no fill at rest; hover picks up the accent fill.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 40px; padding: 0 16px; border: 0; border-radius: 10px; background: transparent; color: hsl(var(--foreground)); font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.01em; transition: background-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), color 200ms; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: hsl(var(--accent) / 0.7); color: hsl(var(--accent-foreground)); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px hsl(var(--ring) / 0.5); }

components.name: Input
components.description: Lit-edge text control; the 3px primary ring on focus is the strongest focus signal in the system.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; min-width: 0; height: 40px; padding: 8px 14px; border: 1px solid hsl(var(--input) / 0.8); border-radius: 10px; background: hsl(var(--background) / 0.75); color: hsl(var(--foreground)); font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 14px; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 hsl(var(--background) / 0.9); backdrop-filter: blur(4px); transition: color 200ms, box-shadow 200ms, border-color 200ms, background-color 200ms; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: hsl(var(--muted-foreground)); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: hsl(var(--ring)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px hsl(var(--ring) / 0.5); } .ds-input[aria-invalid="true"] { border-color: hsl(var(--destructive)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px hsl(var(--destructive) / 0.2); }

components.name: Card
components.description: Flat raised slate, hairline-edged, shadow-xs at rest; hover tightens the border, never lifts.
components.html:
Provider
Anthropic — native adapter, priority 1.
components.css: .ds-card { border: 1px solid hsl(var(--border)); border-radius: 16px; background: hsl(var(--card)); color: hsl(var(--card-foreground)); padding: 16px; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.05); transition: border-color 150ms ease; } .ds-card:hover { border-color: hsl(var(--border) / 0.8); } .ds-card-title { font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 18px; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.375; } .ds-card-body { margin-top: 6px; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 14px; color: hsl(var(--muted-foreground)); line-height: 1.5; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Signature labeled chip — color is redundant; the text label and role=status are the signal. Shown in the HTTP GET variant.
components.css: .ds-badge-status { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; padding: 2px 8px; border: 1px solid hsl(var(--action-blue) / 0.3); border-radius: 9999px; background: hsl(var(--action-blue) / 0.15); color: hsl(var(--action-blue)); font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.25; white-space: nowrap; }

components.name: Nav Item
components.description: Sidebar nav item in its active state — a 2px gradient indicator line is the one colored >1px stripe in the system.
components.html: Providers
components.css: .ds-nav-item { position: relative; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; min-height: 44px; min-width: 44px; padding: 10px 12px; border-radius: 12px; background: transparent; color: hsl(var(--sidebar-foreground)); font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: hsl(var(--sidebar-accent) / 0.7); } .ds-nav-item svg { width: 16px; height: 16px; flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-nav-item-active { background: hsl(var(--sidebar-accent) / 0.95); } .ds-nav-item-active::before { content: ""; position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; bottom: 0; width: 2px; border-radius: 0 9999px 9999px 0; background: linear-gradient(to bottom, hsl(var(--sidebar-primary)), hsl(var(--sidebar-primary) / 0.6)); } .ds-nav-item-active svg { transform: scale(1.1); }

components.name: Color-Tinted Icon Container
components.description: Signature treatment for the icon beside a page title or section heading — a flat, tinted, lightly-ringed tile with a top sheen. Primary variant shown.
components.css: .ds-icon-container { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-height: 44px; min-width: 44px; padding: 10px; border-radius: 16px; } .ds-icon-primary { background: linear-gradient(135deg, hsl(var(--primary) / 0.2), hsl(var(--primary) / 0.1), hsl(var(--primary) / 0.05)); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 hsl(var(--primary) / 0.26), 0 0 0 1px hsl(var(--primary) / 0.3); } .ds-icon-container svg { width: 18px; height: 18px; color: hsl(var(--foreground)); }

components.name: Range Slider
components.description: Signature control for Smart Routing mode-weight sliders — thumb scales on hover, neutralized under reduced motion.
components.css: .ds-range { appearance: none; -webkit-appearance: none; width: 100%; height: 8px; border-radius: 9999px; background: hsl(var(--muted)); } .ds-range::-webkit-slider-thumb { -webkit-appearance: none; appearance: none; width: 16px; height: 16px; border: 2px solid hsl(var(--background)); border-radius: 9999px; background: hsl(var(--primary)); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.25); cursor: pointer; transition: transform 150ms ease; } .ds-range::-webkit-slider-thumb:hover { transform: scale(1.12); } .ds-range::-webkit-slider-thumb:active { transform: scale(0.96); } .ds-range::-webkit-slider-thumb:focus-visible { box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px hsl(var(--background)), 0 0 0 4px hsl(var(--ring)); outline: none; } .ds-range::-moz-range-thumb { width: 16px; height: 16px; border: 2px solid hsl(var(--background)); border-radius: 9999px; background: hsl(var(--primary)); cursor: pointer; transition: transform 150ms ease; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-range::-webkit-slider-thumb, .ds-range::-moz-range-thumb { transition: none; } .ds-range::-webkit-slider-thumb:hover, .ds-range::-webkit-slider-thumb:active, .ds-range::-moz-range-thumb:hover, .ds-range::-moz-range-thumb:active { transform: none; } }

components.name: Code Block
components.description: Quiet progressive-gray code surface — rounded-xl wrapper with a header bar one step lighter; JSON syntax renders structure at low chroma.
components.css: .ds-code-block { border: 1px solid hsl(var(--code-border)); border-radius: 16px; background: hsl(var(--code-bg)); font-family: var(--font-mono); overflow: hidden; } .ds-code-block-header { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; padding: 8px 16px; border-bottom: 1px solid hsl(var(--code-border)); background: hsl(var(--code-header-bg)); color: hsl(var(--muted-foreground)); font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 12px; } .ds-code-block-pre { margin: 0; padding: 16px; overflow-x: auto; font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.625; color: hsl(var(--foreground) / 0.9); } .ds-code-key { color: hsl(var(--json-key)); font-weight: 500; } .ds-code-string { color: hsl(var(--json-string)); }

narrative.overview:
LLM Proxy's admin UI is an infrastructure instrument panel — a dark, monochrome console an operator reads mid-incident and trusts on the first glance. It pairs the discipline of editorial typography (Space Grotesk display, Manrope body, IBM Plex Mono for every number and code value) with the restraint of a telemetry surface: tonal layering, hairline borders, and ambient glow in place of ornament. The operator is technical, time-pressed, and often a stranger deploying the proxy for the first time, so the system earns trust through precision, not decoration.

The palette is monochrome editorial — deep cool-neutral voids in dark mode, crisp near-white in light mode — with a barely-perceptible hue tinting system reserved for semantic differentiation only: HTTP methods, status, and action types. Saturation is deliberately low; color never decorates, it disambiguates. The atmosphere is built from two fixed layers behind every screen: a trio of soft radial foreground-glints and a faint 42px grid masked toward the viewport center — present enough to read as a designed surface, quiet enough never to compete with data.

This system explicitly rejects the generic 2026 AI-tool aesthetic (cream/sand warm-neutral bodies, gradient-text headlines, identical icon-card grids, big-number hero-metric templates), loud SaaS gradients, playful/consumer affordances, and circa-2008 enterprise chrome. It is dark-first: dark mode is the primary experience and the canonical reference for every token; light mode is a complete, first-class translation, not an afterthought.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first monochrome with cool-neutral (220°) undertones; light mode is a crisp mirror.
Editorial type pairing: geometric Space Grotesk display + humanist Manrope body + IBM Plex Mono for data.
Flat-by-default surfaces; depth via tonal background steps + 1px hairline borders, never structural drop shadows.
Low-saturation semantic tints (violet/blue/amber/rose/teal + status + syntax) — always paired with text or icon, never color-only.
Motion is exponential ease-out (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)), 150–500ms, GPU-only, and globally neutralized under prefers-reduced-motion.
Tabular-numeric monospace for every metric, token count, cost, and timestamp.

rules.name: The Monochrome-First Rule
rules.body: Black, white, and the cool-neutral slate ramp carry 90%+ of any screen. Action/status tints are permitted only on badges, icon containers, metric values, and hover glows — never as section backgrounds, button colors (except destructive), or large fills.

rules.name: The Tint, Not the Hue Rule
rules.body: Status and HTTP colors render at low alpha (/15 background, /25–30 border) with the full token as text. The badge is a labeled chip, not a swatch; the text label and role=status are the primary signal.

rules.name: The Cool-Neutral Undertone Rule
rules.body: Every neutral token carries hue 220° at very low chroma (3–14%). Never introduce a true-gray (0 0%) or warm-neutral (hue 30–100) — both break the cool-console atmosphere.

rules.name: The Quiet Syntax Rule
rules.body: The JSON and code palettes differentiate structure at low chroma for scanning — and only on code surfaces (JSON viewers, highlighted snippets, code blocks). Never reuse syntax tokens for badges, chart series, or fills; a rainbow syntax theme is a defect, not a feature.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Space Grotesk + Manrope + IBM Plex Mono is the whole system. Never introduce a fourth family. A number or code value set in Manrope is a defect.

rules.name: The Mono-Data Rule
rules.body: Every numeric value — tokens, cost, latency, counts, timestamps, status codes, HTTP methods — is set in IBM Plex Mono with tabular-nums.

rules.name: The Display Restraint Rule
rules.body: Display weight is 600 in-app, sizes cap at text-2xl (1.5rem) for page titles, and emphasis comes from weight + size in a single solid color — never from background-clip: text or a gradient.

rules.name: The One-Console Rule
rules.body: Management pages are one seamless surface — sticky header, flush toolbar, scrollable body — separated only by border-b/60 hairlines. Never wrap a console table in an outer Card.

rules.name: The Page-Header Anchor Rule
rules.body: Every route opens with exactly one page-header (tinted icon container + brand-heading title + muted description + actions).

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadows appear only as a response to state (hover, elevation, focus) or as the constrained section-card / auth-mark exceptions. Never pair a 1px border with a 16px+ blur drop shadow on the same element.

rules.name: The Tonal-Step Rule
rules.body: When separating two surfaces, step the background token (background → card → muted) before reaching for a shadow. A 1px border hairline plus a tonal step is the default depth recipe.

rules.name: The Radius Cap Rule
rules.body: Cards and panels cap at rounded-xl (16px). Save full-pill for tags and status chips, rounded-lg (12px) for nav items. No 24/28/32/40px card radii, no pill buttons.

rules.name: The One 2px Stripe Rule
rules.body: The only colored >1px stripe in the system is the 2px active-nav gradient indicator. Never use a colored border-left/right accent stripe on cards, list items, or alerts.

dos: Do set every numeric value — tokens, cost, latency, counts, timestamps, status codes — in IBM Plex Mono with tabular-nums (.text-data inline, .text-metric for large stats).
Do convey depth with tonal background steps (--card over --background, --muted/5 page tint) and 1px --border hairlines; reserve shadow for shadow-xs at rest and ambient glow on hover.
Do render status and HTTP semantics as labeled StatusBadge chips at /15 tint + /25–30 border, with role=status and a text label as the primary signal.
Do use the config-page-reveal entrance on every page and the stagger-children / row-stagger cascades on first render — and let the global prefers-reduced-motion rule neutralize them.
Do keep display tracking at -0.02em (floor -0.04em), display weight 600 in-app, and page titles at text-xl sm:text-2xl.
Do hit WCAG AA on both themes: tune --muted-foreground for readability, never lighten muted text for elegance, and bump dark-mode body line-height to 1.55–1.6.
Do keep touch targets ≥44px (min-h-11 min-w-11) on nav and mobile controls.
Do render JSON and code with the syntax palette on code surfaces only — subtle chroma that reads as structure, never a rainbow theme.
donts: Don't make it playful/consumer — no cute illustrations, mascots, gamification, or celebratory confetti. This is infrastructure. (PRODUCT.md anti-reference.)
Don't ship boring/outdated admin panels — no dense gray-on-gray tables, no circa-2008 enterprise chrome, no cluttered everything-on-one-screen dashboards. (PRODUCT.md anti-reference.)

Don't use loud color accents — no saturated SaaS gradients, no neon, no rainbow status badges. Color is a subtle low-saturation tinting system for semantic differentiation, never decoration. (PRODUCT.md anti-reference.)

Don't ship the generic 2026 AI-tool aesthetic — no cream/sand warm-neutral body backgrounds, no gradient-text headlines, no identical icon+heading+text card grids, no big-number hero-metric template. This is monochrome editorial, not warm SaaS. (PRODUCT.md anti-reference.)
Don't pair a 1px border with a 16px+ blur drop shadow on the same element (the ghost-card pattern). Pick a tonal step or shadow-xs, never a wide decorative shadow.
Don't over-round — cards and panels cap at rounded-xl (16px); save full-pill for tags and status chips, rounded-lg (12px) for nav items. No 24/28/32/40px card radii.

Don't use border-left/border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe on cards, list items, or alerts. The 2px active nav indicator is the one exception, and it is a dedicated active-state affordance, not decoration.

Don't use glassmorphism decoratively. backdrop-blur-sm appears only on outline buttons, inputs, and the login-screen auth-input/auth-mark — a deliberate, constrained set, never a default card treatment.
Don't use background-clip: text with a gradient. Display emphasis comes from weight and size, in a single solid color.
Don't put a tiny uppercase tracked eyebrow above every page section. The tracked eyebrow is reserved for the three nav section groups only.
Don't set a metric or number in Manrope, or introduce a fourth type family. Space Grotesk + Manrope + IBM Plex Mono is the whole system.
Don't introduce true-gray (0 0%) or warm-neutral (hue 30–100) tokens. Every neutral carries the 220° cool undertone.
Don't animate layout properties. Motion is transform/opacity only, exponential ease-out (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)), 150–500ms, with a reduced-motion alternative on every animation.
Don't reuse the JSON/code syntax tokens outside code surfaces — no rainbow syntax themes, no syntax-colored badges or chart series.
